newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases on hesitant trade.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases on hesitant trade.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index eased marginally on hesitant trading on key shares across the board, bourse officials said.
The index shed 7.06 points to 3469.38. Turnover was posted at 36.609 million shillings on 803,875 shares compared to 18.599 shillings on 446,972 shares.
"Investors are sitting on the sidelines. Speculators suffered a fair disappointment on Friday after Barclays Bank and Standard Chartered Bank Kenya announced their results," a broker said.
He added that as a result, prices in related shares especially financials had eased as the disappointment spread through the market.
Barclays gained 2.0 shillings to close at 111 while Standard Chartered eased to 50 from 51.50. Kenya Commercial Bank eased to 94 from 95.
Bourse officials said investors were bargain-hunting, which pushed prices down marginally.
A special deal in Sasini Tea & Coffee on the one-hour hold board pushed the price up to 75 from 62. Rea Vipingo was unchanged at 10.
The agriculturals posted marginally improved results following disappointing figures in 1995.

Brooke Bond announced a profit of 214 million shillings before tax for the year ended December 31, 1996, which was 283 percent increase from 1995, while Limuru Tea Company posted a profit of 11 million shillings before tax from seven million shillings in the previous year.
Despite the improved results, a statement by Brooke Bond blamed difficult trading conditions on a strong Kenya shilling and the high cost of borrowing.
But a market analyst said: "A strong and stable shilling cannot be blamed entirely for less-than-projected results because in the long run it helps long-term investors."
"In fact part of the reason why foreign investors are investing in the market is because of a stable shilling," another broker said.
Brooke Bond and Limuru Tea did not trade on Tuesday.
Regent Undervalued Assets Africa Fund is set for listing on the NSE on Thursday. It will be the first international fund to be listed at the NSE and simultaneously in Botswana and Dublin.
